open_points.subject: store_spool.spool_entry_name
open_points.question: What inputs does this capability take, what kind of name does it return, and can it fail?
options: Take a SpooledFileKey and return a bounded relative entry name
Take a spool root plus SpooledFileKey and return a full path
Keep it private and remove it from the public capabilities
open_points.default_guess: Take a SpooledFileKey and return an injective bounded relative entry name with no failure.

open_points.subject: store_spool.spool_attempt_prefix
open_points.question: Which attempt facts form the input, what does the returned prefix denote, and can callers use it as a path or only as an opaque deletion key?
options: Take run, node, map index and attempt number and return an opaque relative prefix
Take a complete SpooledFileKey and derive its attempt prefix
Keep attempt deletion internal to publish_spool_entry
open_points.default_guess: Take run_id, producer_node_id, optional map_index and attempt_number and return an opaque relative prefix.

open_points.subject: store_spool.publish_spool_entry
open_points.text: publishing one file complete, fsynced and digest-checked by a temporary and a rename, replacing a file at the same position; the two spool ceilings of A20, checked on publishing, and discarding every file of the refused attempt
open_points.question: What are this operation's exact inputs and outputs, who supplies or computes digest and size, how the current run total is obtained, and does this call itself discard the attempt atomically on a ceiling refusal or require a later discard_spool_attempt call?
options: One call takes spool root, key, bytes and expected facts, checks both ceilings, publishes or discards the whole attempt, and returns the verified facts
One call only publishes and reports a ceiling refusal; store then calls discard_spool_attempt
The caller supplies the current run-byte total instead of store_spool deriving it
open_points.default_guess: One call takes the spool location, SpooledFileKey, bytes, expected digest and size; store_spool derives the current run total and on a ceiling refusal removes the entire attempt before returning refusal.

open_points.subject: store_spool.read_spool_entry
open_points.text: reading a file back checked against a digest and size
open_points.question: What record facts and location inputs are required, what bytes or facts are returned, and how are a missing entry, symlink, digest mismatch, size mismatch and ordinary I/O failure distinguished for store to map them to store.read_value_bytes outcomes?
options: Take spool root, key, expected digest and size and return verified bytes or typed failure
Take a SpooledFile record and derive all expected facts from it
Return only bytes and collapse every failure into one error
open_points.default_guess: Take the spool location, SpooledFileKey, expected digest and expected size and return verified bytes, with typed missing, symlink, integrity and I/O failures for store to map.

open_points.subject: store_spool.discard_spool_attempt
open_points.question: What identifies the attempt, whether removal is idempotent, what happens to temporary files of that attempt, and what result is returned when some removal fails?
options: Take an attempt identity, remove its completed and temporary entries idempotently, and report I/O failure
Take an attempt prefix produced by spool_attempt_prefix and remove matching completed entries only
Use it only internally during publish_spool_entry and expose no callable capability
open_points.default_guess: Take the attempt identity, remove all completed and temporary entries for it idempotently, and return a typed I/O failure if complete removal cannot be confirmed.

open_points.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_group
open_points.question: What is a spool group, which identifier names it, whether removal of an absent group succeeds, and how a partial or failed removal is reported to store.remove_run_spool?
options: A group is one run, named by run_id; removal is idempotent and reports I/O failure
A group is an arbitrary generated directory key supplied by store
Removal is best-effort and never reports failure
open_points.default_guess: A group is one run named by run_id; an absent group succeeds and an incomplete removal returns an I/O failure that store.remove_run_spool maps to internal_error.

open_points.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_temporaries
open_points.text: removing the temporaries an interrupted publish left
open_points.question: What scope is scanned, when store calls it, whether it also validates or rejects links encountered during the scan, and whether failure stops store.open_store or is ignored like failure to remove an ended run's spool?
options: Scan the whole spool area during open_store; any symlink or cleanup failure fails startup
Scan one run directory supplied by store and continue after cleanup failures
Remove only explicitly named temporary entries
open_points.default_guess: Scan the whole spool area during store.open_store, refuse any symlink, and fail startup if temporary cleanup cannot be completed.
